## Linear Algebra

### with special symbols
```{=typst}
#set math.equation(numbering: "(1)")

$
forall v, w in V, alpha in KK: alpha dot (v + w) = alpha v + alpha w
$
```

### unicode

$$
∀ v, w ∈ V, α ∈ 𝕂: α ⋅ (v + w) = α v + α w
$$

## Draw

```{=typst}
// With content.

#rect( fill: blue.lighten(80%))[ This is a rectangle ] 

#polygon(
  fill: blue.lighten(80%),
  stroke: red,
  (20%, 0pt),
  (60%, 0pt),
  (80%, 2cm),
  (0%,  2cm))


#rect(radius: 15%, height: 15%, width: 10%, fill: yellow)

% tiny rectangle
#polygon.regular(vertices: 4)

% tiny triangle
#polygon(
  fill: blue, 
  stroke: red,
  (0pt, 0pt), 
  (10pt, 10pt), 
  (0pt, 10pt))

#v(1cm)

```

Each polygon point is an (x, y) pair of relative lengths. So besides percentages, you can use absolute Typst lengths—such as pt, mm, cm, in, or em—and you can mix them
x-y  begins upper level (0,0),  positive x is then down

### Polygons

```{=typst}

#v(1cm)
#polygon(
  (1cm, 0pt),
  (0pt, 2cm),
  (3cm, 2cm),
)

#v(1cm)

/*
% huge
#polygon(
  (50%, 0pt),     // halfway across; at top
  (0pt, 2cm),     // left edge; 2 cm down
  (100%, 2cm),    // right edge; 2 cm down
)

#v(1cm)
#polygon(
(50% + 5pt, 1cm))
*/

```

### Functions
**Functions begin with pound ** \ 
Followed by args (in parenthesis) and content in square brackets
```{=typst}
#lorem(20)
````
***
**More function examples:**
```{=typst}
#list[
  All that markup is just a #emph[syntax sugar] over functions!


#text(size: 0.8em)[This is content]
#text(orange)[orange content], but this is regular content.
#link("https://typst.app/docs/reference/")[link to Official Reference].
]
```



### Block with background color and inset 
```{=typst}

#set align(center)
#block(
  //fill: rgb("f58025"),
  fill: silver,
  inset: 14pt,
  width: 100%,
[Can use typ file, but then use `typst` ecosystem to render]
)
#set align(left)
```

### use a variable
```{=typst}

#let jr = [jim]

The variable 'jr' holds value #jr

#table(
  columns: (1fr, 1fr),
  [variable], [Typst],
  [jr], jr,
)
```

### simple quote block
```{=typst}
#quote(block: true)[
  So #text(red)[_that_] allows me to write
  _literally anything_ in things
  I pass to #underline[functions]!
]
```
### Box + a show function, a trigger, then action: 
```{=typst}
#show emph: set text(blue) // emph renders as blue
#show "typst": set text(orange)
#box(stroke: gray, inset: 1em)[typst should be _taught_]
```
